summary: Issei Yamakawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Sophia University and completed a master's program at Aichi Gakuin University.
Isshin Teshima is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 2015 and 2026.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology who studied at Teachers College and taught Qian Lin. She is attested as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington in 2026.

Ivan Minayev (1840–1890) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1858–1862), taught at its Faculty of Oriental Studies (~1871–1890), and instructed Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, Dmitry Kudryavsky, and Sergey Oldenburg.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (1840–1890) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and under Albrecht Weber (1863), later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Ives Goddard (1941–2025) was a linguist who studied at Harvard College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1963–1969). He held posts at Harvard (~1969–1979), the Smithsonian Institution (~1979), and the National Museum of Natural History (~1979).
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa (1970–1988), and taught David P. Jackson.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University (-2003) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer (1929–2004) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Charles University (attested 1960) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology (attested 1970).

Iwao Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held posts at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2000), the Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (all attested 2026).

Iwao Nakajima studied under Nichiki Kimura and earned a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as editor-in-chief at Sandhaan (attested 1999).
Iwao Shima (1950–2007) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya University and held posts at Kanazawa University, where he is attested from 1992 and as a professor in 2003.

Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1987–1997). At Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, she was an assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023).

Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in Japanology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, taught Qian Lin, and is attested as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington in 2026.

J. A. B. van Buitenen (1928–1979) was an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (1946–1953). He held posts at Deccan College (1954–1956), Utrecht University (1959–1961), and the University of Chicago (1957, 1959, 1961, 1964).
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. In 1996, he was attested as a professor at the University of Colombo and held an attested post at SOAS University of London.

J. Gordon Melton is a religious studies scholar who studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history and archaeology. He studied under William Dwight Whitney and served as a professor at Brown University, attested in 1897.

J. J. C. Smart (1920–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1938–1946) and The Queen's College, Oxford (~1946–1948). He held posts at the University of Adelaide (~1950–1972), La Trobe University (~1972–1976), and Australian National University (~1976–1985).
J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1891–1925) and taught Surendranath Dasgupta.
